clue.text: Academic qualification's so fundamental

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a first university degree
sic is Latin for 'thus' or 'so', used to mark a quoted error

explanation.surface: A remark that a degree is so basic an entry requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic is elementary and at the root of things, which is what fundamental means.

clue.text: Beauty could be a big disappointment

definitions.meaning: a stunning, attractive woman, as in 'blonde ___'
a shattering piece of news that upsets everyone

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman turns out to be a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is both a strikingly attractive woman and a shocking, upsetting surprise.

clue.text: Discovers a craniologist hoarding bones

indicators.note: the phrase hoards, or keeps stored inside it, the answer's letters

explanation.surface: An expert on skulls finds a stash of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacra is the plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Customer's awfully nice and tall

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A shopper is described as very nice and tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliental is the adjective for clients, so it means relating to a customer.

clue.text: Claimed old fogey's first to get squeezed out

indicators.note: the outer word is made to get the other pieces placed within it

parts.note: something squeezed out is pressed out

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An old fogey claims to have been the first to be forced out of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' places O (old) and F (first of 'fogey's') inside PRESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have professed something is to have claimed or declared it openly.

clue.text: Duo put together piano tune

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Two musicians compose a piano melody together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two, the same as a duo.

clue.text: Likely location of roof-rack at start of drive south?

parts.note: a roof-rack is fitted on the car

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A roof-rack goes on before a drive south.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the cards is probable, likely to happen, as if foretold by fortune-telling cards.

clue.text: European Union's first to congratulate top mathematician

parts.note: EU is the abbreviation for European Union

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: a lid is a top or cover

explanation.surface: Europe is the first to congratulate a leading mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid, the Greek geometer, is one of history's greatest mathematicians.

clue.text: Possibly eat this with grated Parmesan for starters

definitions.text: Possibly eat this with grated Parmesan for starters

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters
the starting letters of the two words are used

explanation.surface: A suggestion to eat a dish topped with grated cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges EAT THIS with G and P, the first letters of 'grated Parmesan'; the whole clue also describes the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is often served with grated Parmesan, which the whole clue suggests.

clue.text: Raised sack holding new currency from abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from the bottom upwards
the sack word holds another letter inside it

parts.note: to sack a town is to raid it

explanation.surface: A sack holding new foreign money is lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts N in RAID, giving RANID; 'Raised' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency of several countries, such as Kuwait and Serbia.

clue.text: A feature film about factory worker, perhaps

indicators.note: the film word goes about, or around, the other pieces

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like a mist on glass
the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A feature film is made about a factory worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature film' reads as one cinema phrase, but 'about' wraps the film word around A and the feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist operates machines, as many factory workers do, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Old movie actor, is out of place in series

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place comes out of the actor's name

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin was a silent-film star
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: An old film star feels out of place in a television series.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking PL from CHAPLIN leaves the letters wanted; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a connected run of things, like a series of events.

clue.text: Makes large numbers of pledges to son

indicators.note: the son is put to, or against, the front of the pledges

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
items pawned are pledged as security for a loan

explanation.surface: A father makes many pledges to his son.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that spawns produces offspring in great quantity, like frogs laying eggs.

clue.text: One dies in pain

definitions.meaning: a pain is an annoying person, a little nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone dies in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Perisher is British slang for a tiresome child or person, a pain, and literally one who perishes.

clue.text: Cake obtained for East End star

definitions.meaning: a sweet bun with dried fruit
Cockney rhyming slang for the sun

explanation.surface: A cake is bought for a celebrity from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney part of London, home of rhyming slang, where 'currant bun' means sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant bun is a sweet roll with currants, and in rhyming slang the sun, a star.

clue.text: More painting outside the university

parts.note: extra means more, additional
a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: More wall art is painted outside the college.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramural courses are run beyond the walls of a university, for outside students.

clue.text: Extremely faithful countryman almost overwhelmed by trial

indicators.note: the countryman is engulfed by the trial word

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a rustic is a country person

explanation.surface: A loyal country fellow is nearly swamped by a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the countryman's last letter and 'overwhelmed by' puts what remains inside the trial word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trustiest is the superlative of trusty, so most reliable, extremely faithful.

clue.text: Stock Exchange speculator standing to lose 50%

indicators.note: losing half the word keeps only its first half

parts.note: standing water is stagnant, not flowing

explanation.surface: A trader's position stands to lose half its value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose 50%' cuts the eight-letter STAGNANT down to its first four letters. A stag buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Stock Exchange a stag applies for new issues to sell on quickly, a type of speculator.

clue.text: Fizzy drink making soldier and general squiffy

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: squiffy means slightly drunk, so the letters stagger about

explanation.surface: A soldier and a general get tipsy on fizzy drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a carbonated soft drink flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: Obtained a recording in which singers can be heard

indicators.note: the recording holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording

indicators.note: can be heard says the word is spoken, giving a spelling with the same sound

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: Someone bought a disc of a choir singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be heard' gives an old word for a body of singers that sounds the same; 'in which' sets it inside the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquired means got or obtained.

clue.text: Oaf left unconscious

parts.note: someone knocked out cold is out

explanation.surface: A boorish man has been left out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is an uncouth, clumsy person, a synonym for oaf.

clue.text: In favour of Channel One showing drama, say

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a duct is a channel or tube
I is the Roman numeral one
a play that is on is showing

explanation.surface: A TV channel is in favour of showing a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel One' reads as a TV station but splits into DUCT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama staged or filmed is a production, given as an example by 'say'.

clue.text: New form of direct debit? The opposite

indicators.note: the word is given a new form, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bank introduces a new kind of direct debit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direct debit' looks like one banking phrase; 'debit' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is the accounting counterpart of debit, its opposite.

clue.text: Making changes to flagging, but not at the front

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: flagging means weakening, faltering

explanation.surface: Changes are being made to a flag, though not at the front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flagging' looks like the hanging of flags; it means faltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering something is changing it, so the phrases match.

clue.text: Language spoken when at college?

indicators.note: spoken means the phrase is said out loud for its sound

parts.note: tec is short for technical college, so at tec

explanation.surface: Which language is spoken while studying at college?
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link. Aztec is a name for Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs of Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztec is the language of the Aztec people, also called Nahuatl.

clue.text: Make a move to capture one bird.

indicators.note: the move word captures, or holds, the other piece

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hunter moves to trap a single bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The budgie, short for budgerigar, is a small pet parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgie is a small Australian parakeet, a kind of bird.

clue.text: I see inside information is supplied

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the information word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Someone notes that information has been provided.
explanation.definitionFit: Given means provided or supplied, as a past participle.

clue.text: Jumper from second-hand market

definitions.meaning: a market for used goods, ___ market

explanation.surface: A sweater bought from a used-goods stall.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a sweater, which misleads here.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a jumping insect, and gives its name to a market selling second-hand goods.

clue.text: Current fashion is teenager's first and last goal

indicators.note: only the word's first and last letters are used

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Teenagers' main aim is to follow the current fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is the prevailing style, what is fashionable at present.

clue.text: See bishops regal building, travelling through part of London

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the letters of regal are built into a new order

parts.note: via means by way of, travelling through

explanation.surface: Bishops travelling through London see a regal building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' sits as an opening link. Belgravia is a wealthy district of central London near Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgravia is an expensive residential district of west central London.

clue.text: Lifeless state of Spanish' region, needing change at the centre

indicators.note: the middle letter of the region is swapped for another

parts.note: Catalonia is a region of north-east Spain, capital Barcelona

explanation.surface: A Spanish region is stagnant and needs central reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The central L of CATALONIA becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia is a stupor in which a person is motionless and unresponsive.

clue.text: Name adopted by accomplished writer

indicators.note: the name is taken into, adopted by, the other word

parts.note: something accomplished is done

explanation.surface: An accomplished author takes a pen-name.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne was the English metaphysical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a 17th-century poet and preacher, hence a writer.
